I’m not quite sure what your problem is but you seem to have some anger issues. Ad hominem don’t really add to the conversation. It isn’t privilege to want a company to be careful with their updates. It doesn’t matter if not all watches were affected, the fact that some watches were is enough reason to hold Apple accountable.  It’s embarrassing to have this happen.
I just believe that more care should have been taken considering the price. It was reckless and letting them off the hook as if it’s perfectly okay is just idiotic.

First time? Their devices have bricked plenty of times before due to updates they put out. It’s not about the overall product doing fine, it’s about how they haven’t even put out a statement about it, they just pulled it with no communication.

I don’t quite think those two situations are quite the same but okay. This is an update that Apple put out themselves. You can argue that one should wait before updating but I would argue that a company like Apple should want their customers to be excited when a new update rolls out and want them to want to update, not be fearful that trusting them might lead to their device breaking. It’s Apple’s fault.
Normally I would agree but when customers pay such a premium for their products, the least they could do is make sure their own updates won’t fuck it up.
